findings: At categorical depth 9 the conversion floor (6/3^9 = 3.05e-4) dominates the oscillator floor by ~4100x, so beta is effectively condition-independent there. The conditioned floor only governs in the Q-dominated regime (short integration times).

checks.check: floor at reference conditions reproduces the published order
checks.detail: beta(ref) = 3.3031e-04 vs published 3.7000e-04; log10 ratio -0.049. dominant term: conv

checks.check: floor rises with temperature (sign)
checks.detail: beta(4C) = 3.303031305209e-04 < beta(37C) = 3.303113365554e-04. Q falls as thermal occupation rises, so the coarsest resolvable boundary grows. Sign only -- magnitude is checked separately.

checks.check: temperature dependence is material (>1%) at depth 9
checks.detail: relative swing 4C->37C = 2.484e-05 (0.002484%). At d=9 floor_conv=3.048e-04 dominates floor_Q=7.414e-08 by 4112x, so beta barely moves. This is the finding: at the depth the address manifold uses, the floor is effectively condition-INDEPENDENT.

checks.check: a depth exists where temperature dependence is material
checks.detail: crossover depth = 15. Above it the combinatorial terms dominate and the floor is effectively condition-independent; below it, conditions govern.

checks.check: floor falls with longer integration (sign)
at short integration the Q term dominates and conditions govern
checks.detail: T_int=1e-12s: floor_Q=2.345e-03 vs floor_conv=3.048e-04; dominant=Q. This is the regime the conditioned floor is about.

checks.check: temperature dependence is material in the Q-dominated regime
checks.detail: relative swing 4C->37C at T_int=1e-12s = 1.034e-01 (10.34%), vs 0.002484% at T_int=1e-3s. The conditioned floor is real, but only where Q dominates.

checks.check: sub-floor difference across conditions is not commensurable
checks.detail: delta 1.321e-04 <= governing floor 3.303e-04 (set by condition 'b'): the two values are one measurement

checks.check: supra-floor difference across conditions is commensurable
checks.detail: delta 1.000e-01 > governing floor 3.303e-04

checks.check: the two floors being compared are actually different
checks.detail: beta(coarse, T_int=1e-15s) = 7.447e-02 vs beta(fine, T_int=1e-1s) = 3.302e-04; ratio 226x. Without this the governance check below would be vacuous -- an earlier version of this suite compared 4C to 37C, whose floors are equal to 11 decimal places, and passed on noise.

checks.check: the coarser floor governs comparability
checks.detail: governing floor 7.447e-02 = the COARSE one (7.447e-02), not the fine one (3.302e-04); limited_by='b'

checks.check: a fine-floor difference is erased by a coarse-floor comparator
checks.detail: delta 6.605e-04 clears the fine floor (3.302e-04) but not the governing coarse floor (7.447e-02): pairing a precise measurement with a sloppy one destroys the precision. This is why conditions must be reported.

checks.check: floor-indistinguishable variants are grouped, not ranked
checks.detail: 7 variants -> 3 distinguishable group(s), sizes [1, 1, 5]. The 5-member group differs by < beta=3.303e-04 and cannot be ranked.

checks.check: genuinely separated variants stay separate
a coarser floor still separates outliers but absorbs the cluster
checks.detail: at beta=3.303e-04: 3 groups [1, 1, 5]; at beta=7.447e-02: 3 groups [1, 1, 5]. The 0.4/1.5 outliers survive a 225x coarser floor because they are ~0.5 apart; the cluster was never resolvable.

checks.check: a sufficiently coarse floor erases all distinctions
checks.detail: at beta=2.345e+00 (> the full 1.1 spread of the plate): 1 group of 7 variants. Every variant is the same measurement; the plate carries no information.

checks.check: group count is monotone in the floor
checks.detail: fine 3 >= ref 3 >= coarse 3
